export const slugify = (input) => {
  let s = input
  s = s.trim()
  s = s.toLowerCase()
  s = s.replace(/\s+/g, '-')
  s = s.slice(0, 40)
  return s
}
fixtures.rationale: slugify threads input through four sequential reassignments of the same binding, each a nameable transformation (trim, lowercase, replace, slice) that could stand alone.
Four consecutive const declarations, each referencing only the binding immediately before it, thread raw through parse, double, clamp, and format as one inline recipe.
The four locally defined steps are already named, but the return statement inlines their composition as a four-deep call pyramid instead of composing them with a pipe or reduce.

export const formatOrderTotal = (order) => {
  let value = order.rawTotal
  value = normalizeWhitespace(value)
  value = applyDiscount(value, order.discountRate)
  value = addTax(value, order.taxRate)
  value = Math.round(value)
  value = formatCurrency(value)
  return value
}
fixtures.rationale: Five distinct order-formatting steps (normalize, discount, tax, round, format) are chained through reassignments of the same binding instead of being composed as named functions.
process composes three sibling named helpers through exactly three levels of nesting, one below the default pyramid threshold of four, so the collector finds no evidence at all.

export const topTen = (items) => {
  return items
    .filter(x => x.active)
    .map(x => x.value)
    .filter(x => x > 0)
    .sort((a, b) => a - b)
    .slice(0, 10)
}
fixtures.rationale: The five-call method chain is already composition: each link is a named, intent-revealing array method, so the long chain is evidence but not the violation.
Two steps computing one tax formula fall below the three-step reassignment threshold and never reach a four-deep call pyramid, so no evidence is produced.
Each const reads directly from order rather than from the previous binding, so no chain forms even though four declarations appear in sequence.
Only one reassignment follows the initial let, one short of the default minSteps of three; a lower minSteps option would turn this into a candidate.
